articles.title: Measles Killed 32 Baiga Children in Madhya Pradesh as Vaccination Lagged
articles.excerpt: In Balaghat's forest blocks, measles-rubella coverage ran between 49% and 70% — far below the WHO's 95% herd-immunity threshold — and distance, migration and fragile trust kept children unprotected.
articles.image_caption: Archival photograph: young Baiga women in traditional dress in India. A measles outbreak in the Baiga community of Balaghat district, Madhya Pradesh, reportedly killed 32 children this year.
articles.nri_angle: The outbreak is a reminder for families in India and abroad to check that children's two measles-rubella doses are complete; local ASHA workers and ANMs can confirm missed doses.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: At 75 and 63, They Married at the Bilaspur Old-Age Home Where They Met
articles.excerpt: Kanhaiya Lal, rescued from a forest after his wife's death, and Sabina, who reached Himachal from Kolkata with no one to claim her, wed at Apna Ghar in Dayoli on November 25 — and will now move to a new home in Nalagarh together.
articles.image_caption: Kanhaiya Lal and Sabina in wedding dress at Apna Ghar Old Age Home in Dayoli, Bilaspur, on November 25, 2026. The two residents of the home married there after meeting as fellow residents.
articles.nri_angle: A story about companionship and care in old age that resonates with diaspora families supporting elderly parents back in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's KochVac TB Vaccine Candidate Targets Human Trials by Mid-2027
articles.excerpt: The protein subunit candidate from IIT Bhubaneswar and the Institute of Life Sciences, patented on November 16 and licensed to TechInvention Lifecare, is being studied as a possible BCG booster — with no human efficacy data yet.
articles.nri_angle: TB remains a major health burden in India; an indigenous booster candidate matters to diaspora families with relatives in high-burden regions.

articles.title: Traditional Indian Diet and Daily Walks Put 60.9% of Early Diabetes Patients Into Remission
articles.excerpt: A six-month programme of familiar Indian food in measured portions and 40 minutes of daily walking achieved remission in 53 of 87 adults with recent-onset type 2 diabetes — in a single-arm study its own authors say now needs a controlled trial.
articles.image_caption: Members of the research team from Chellaram Diabetes Institute, Pune, and Dr Kale's Diabetes and Psychiatry Clinic, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, who ran the six-month dietary intervention study. The study reported remission in 60.9% of participants with early type 2 diabetes.

sources.label: PubMed — LHMC diet and structured exercise for diabetes remission in early type 2 diabetes (study abstract)

articles.nri_angle: South Asians develop type 2 diabetes earlier and at lower body weights; a remission programme built on the food Indian families already eat — tested in Pune and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar — is directly relevant to diaspora readers managing early diabetes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi AQI Hits 511 as November Becomes Most Polluted Month on Record
articles.excerpt: PM2.5 reached 22.1 times the WHO guideline on Sunday morning after a Saturday peak of 577; AQI.in estimates the exposure at 12.5 cigarettes a day and advises residents to stay indoors.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers with parents in Delhi: move exercise indoors, run purifiers, use N95s outdoors, and postpone elderly family members' non-essential outdoor errands while AQI stays severe.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Diabetes Remission in 90 Days? Doctors Explain What the Term Really Means
articles.excerpt: Remission means an HbA1c below 6.5% held for at least three months without medication — a definition, not a deadline. Doctors explain the weight-loss mechanism, the South Asian risk caveat, and why real-world remission rates are far lower than trial headlines.
articles.image_caption: A person checks blood glucose with a finger-prick glucometer. Doctors say type 2 diabetes remission means an HbA1c below 6.5 percent sustained for at least three months without glucose-lowering medication.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians develop metabolic problems at lower BMI levels, doctors note, so diaspora readers should weigh waist size and lipids alongside weight when judging remission prospects.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Winter, Pollution and Children's Lungs: Why Doctors Want Extra Care This November
articles.excerpt: Children's developing lungs, faster breathing rates and immature immune systems make November's pollution peak especially risky, paediatric specialists say. The warning signs that mean a cough is no longer 'just seasonal' are specific.
articles.image_caption: Smog over Delhi during winter, when air pollution peaks and doctors warn of risks to children's lungs.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families visiting India with children this winter, the same precautions apply from the first day: check the AQI before outdoor plans and keep asthma medication in hand baggage.

articles.title: Titan Diwali Film Honours 16,000 Karigars Who Craft India's Festive Jewellery
articles.excerpt: 'Sukriya, Karigar' follows four artisans whose work becomes family milestones — and behind the film sits a decade of documented change in how Titan's jewellery karigars work.

sources.label: Titan Company announcement via Sociapa News

articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families buying gold for Diwali, the film and the audited artisan standards behind it offer a concrete way to judge the jewellery they gift and wear.

articles.title: Yoga-Based Cardiac Rehab Improved Quality of Life in Heart Failure Trial
articles.excerpt: In 3,492 adults in India, Yoga-CaRe improved quality-of-life scores and walking distance, but death, hospitalisation or stroke was 21.0% versus 22.8% — not statistically significant.
articles.nri_angle: A supervised yoga-based rehab model tested in India may inform care options for diaspora families managing heart failure.
